Wingate from subfossil material found in the Pleistocene and Holocene deposits in caves and ponds of Bermuda.","title":"Bermuda night heron"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Its anatomy was rather similar to its living relative, the yellow-crowned night heron (\"N. violacea\"), but it had a heavier bill, a more massive skull and more robust hind limbs.","title":"Bermuda night heron"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" The specialization of the bill and the hind limbs showed that it was apparently adapted to the feeding on land crabs.","title":"Bermuda night heron"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" There are also early historian reports referring to that species.","title":"Bermuda night heron"},{"sentence_id":6,"text":" It possibly became extinct due to the settlement of the Bermuda islands in the 17th century.","title":"Bermuda night heron"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The expression \"Giant of Castelnau\" refers to three bone fragments (a humerus, tibia, and femoral mid-shaft) discovered by Georges Vacher de Lapouge in 1890 in the sediment used to cover a Bronze Age burial tumulus, and then possibly dating back to the Neolithic.","title":"Giant of Castelnau"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" According to de Lapouge, the fossil bones may belong to one of the largest humans known to have existed.","title":"Giant of Castelnau"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" He estimated from the bone size that the human may have been about 3.50 metres tall.","title":"Giant of Castelnau"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" No modern peer-reviewed study has been published about the alleged giant bone fragments.","title":"Giant of Castelnau"}],"peer_messages":["Unverified peer answer: noanswer"],"previous_answer":"noanswer","question":"How many degrees and minutes south of the equator are the bone fragments of the extinct Ascension night heron found?"}
